meta.title: VibeIDE — an open AI code editor with no subscription
meta.description: A VS Code fork with AI inside the editor: any model, an agent with autopilot, no subscription and no telemetry, MIT source
lang.label: Language
lang.ru.name: Русский
lang.en.name: English
hero.title: AI inside the editor
hero.lead:
No subscription and no telemetry
Your keys and your models, local ones included
Everything the agent sees and does stays under your control
hero.note:
No account
Extensions from Open VSX
Windows and macOS
hero.ide.aria: VibeIDE window: the agent got a task, edits files and runs the tests
hero.ide.ask: Add a dark theme and tests for it
facts.free.text: You pay only your model provider, for the tokens you use
facts.telemetry.text: No telemetry, keys live in the OS keychain
facts.models.text: Built in out of the box, your own one is a single file away
models.title:
A new model today
Not in the next editor release
models.lead:
The {file} file adds, overrides or turns off a provider and its models
They work on par with the built-in ones, and the model list comes live from the API
No key — run models locally with Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM
models.sphere: A sphere of providers: the model providers built into VibeIDE orbit the editor
models.snippet: Example: your own model gateway in one file
why.title: Why VibeIDE and not Cursor, Windsurf or Copilot
why.lead:
The same jobs done with no monthly fee
And without sending your code to the editor vendor
features.title: What it does
features.lead:
Not a list of checkmarks
But the reasons this editor was written
features.autopilot.title: An agent with autopilot
features.autopilot.text:
Takes a task to the end on its own: multi-agent orchestration with locks
Plans survive an IDE restart, and on a limit the team saves its work and carries on
features.tokens.title: Token savings
features.tokens.text:
Terminal and MCP output is compressed before it reaches the context, errors and results are kept word for word
You see how many tokens were saved
features.voice.title: Offline voice input
features.voice.text:
Dictation into chat, editor and terminal, recognised right on your computer
Russian and English, the audio goes nowhere
features.preview.title: Preview without a deploy
features.preview.text:
Static files, a framework dev server or a Docker setup right in the IDE
Click an element of the page and a draft of the edit is already in the chat
features.spec.title: A spec before the code
features.spec.text:
A big feature is described by a spec first: what we build and how
During the build, edits outside the declared scope are paused, so the agent does not spread over the project
features.watch.title: Videos and calls in the chat
features.watch.text:
The /watch command downloads a video, cuts frames at scene changes and transcribes the audio locally
The model sees what was on screen instead of retelling subtitles
features.privacy.title: Private by default
features.privacy.text:
No Microsoft telemetry, and secret detection runs before anything goes to a model
A session token limit and a context gauge, so the bill is never a surprise
features.compat.title: Compatible with VS Code
features.compat.text:
Your habits, shortcuts and extensions stay with you
Open VSX without a Microsoft account and an IntelliJ-style keymap for those coming from JetBrains
autopilot.title:
You set the task
The agent takes it to the end
autopilot.lead:
Plan, edits, tests and review, without a nudge at every step
A model limit does not wipe the work: progress is saved and the agent carries on where it stopped
autopilot.aria: The agent at work: plan, edits, tests, a model limit, carrying on and a finished result
autopilot.task: Task: a dark theme for the settings
family.title:
Three tools
One set of rules
family.lead:
Both IDEs read the same project rules and settings
And the agents' memory links them across sessions and machines
family.vibeide: An editor built on VS Code with its own agent
family.vibeidea: An IDE on the IntelliJ platform for PHP and TypeScript
family.vibememory: Shared memory for agents: context outlives sessions and machines
install.title: Up and running in a minute
install.s1.title: Download and run
install.s1.text:
Windows — the .exe installer or the winget command
macOS — a .dmg image for Apple Silicon
install.s2.title: Connect a model
install.s2.text:
A key for Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible server
Or no key at all, with local models
install.s3.title: Open a project and ask
install.s3.text:
The agent sees the codebase, edits files and runs the tests
And at any moment you see what it is about to do
releases.title: Latest builds
releases.all: All versions and release notes — on GitHub
firstRun.title: First launch: the system will ask you to confirm
firstRun.lead:
The installer is not signed with a publisher certificate: it is paid and tied to a company
The system says it cannot verify the publisher, not that it found anything bad
You confirm it once
firstRun.windows.s1: In the SmartScreen window click «More info» — at first only «Don't run» is visible
firstRun.windows.note: Or install from the Microsoft catalogue, with no warnings
firstRun.macos.s1:
Drag the app to Applications and launch it, then click «Done» in the «Not Opened» window
Without this attempt the button you need will not appear
firstRun.macos.s2: Open «System Settings → Privacy & Security» and click «Open Anyway»
firstRun.macos.s3: Confirm with Touch ID or your password and launch VibeIDE again — an «Open» button appears
firstRun.macos.note: Control-click → «Open» no longer helps in these versions: Apple removed this bypass starting with Sequoia
firstRun.more: The terminal way and checksum verification — in the first launch guide
honesty.title: Honest about platforms
honesty.text:
Windows and macOS on Apple Silicon are built and published with every release
Linux builds from source for now, ready packages are in progress
cta.title: Take the whole editor
cta.lead:
Open source, no subscription, the vendor never sees your code
One installer, and then it is just you, your project and your models
